heroText: Dodoma is Tanzania's official capital, a compact highland city built around the Bunge (National Assembly) and the country's fledgling wine industry. First-time visitors should view the Bunge building's public grounds, sample local vintages from the Dodoma Vineyards, and browse everyday goods at Uhindini Market. Dodoma Airport connects the city domestically, and Dodoma makes an interesting stop for travelers curious about Tanzania's planned-capital story.

areas.name: City Centre / Uhuru
areas.text: The city centre around Uhuru and Bunge holds government offices, banks and the main shopping streets, easiest for a short stay.

areas.name: Area C
areas.text: Area C is a residential district near shops and mid-range guesthouses, a practical base within easy reach of downtown offices.

areas.name: Kikuyu
areas.text: Kikuyu sits near the University of Dodoma's campus, useful for academic visitors and budget-friendly stays.

areas.name: Uhindini
areas.text: Uhindini is Dodoma's main commercial and market district, packed with shops, textiles and everyday goods.

airports.name: Dodoma Airport (DOD)
airports.text: Dodoma Airport sits a short drive from the city centre, with domestic flights connecting to Dar es Salaam and other Tanzanian cities.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Dodoma Airport (DOD) and central Dodoma before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in the city centre near Uhuru and Bunge for an easy first stay close to government offices and shops, or choose Area C for a quieter residential base. Kikuyu suits academic visitors near the university, while Uhindini works well for travelers focused on markets and shopping.
hotelIntro: Dodoma hotel choice depends on purpose: the city centre suits government and business visitors wanting proximity to the Bunge, Area C suits longer, quieter stays, and Kikuyu or Uhindini suit academic visitors and shoppers respectively.
rentalCars: A rental car helps for visiting Dodoma's vineyards and surrounding countryside, though the compact city centre is easily covered on foot or by taxi.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose the city centre near Uhuru and Bunge for an easy stay close to government offices, banks and restaurants.

travelTips.title: Wine tasting
travelTips.text: Set aside time for a Dodoma Vineyards tasting, since the region is Tanzania's main wine-producing area.

travelTips.title: Airport transfers
travelTips.text: Arrange a taxi from Dodoma Airport in advance, as the domestic terminal has limited ride-hailing availability.

travelTips.title: Government access
travelTips.text: Check current visitor rules before attempting to tour the Bunge grounds, since access can vary during parliamentary sessions.

history.text: The city, designed over 2,500 acres (1,000 hectares), was meant to be "the chief village in a nation of villages", built at a human scale meant to be experienced on foot.

history.label: 20th century
history.text: 20th century Originally a small market town known as Idodomya, the modern Dodoma was founded in 1907 by German colonists during construction of the Tanzanian central railway.
The site, the Dodoma region, had been looked at as a potential new capital as early as 1915 by the then colonial power Germany, in 1932 by the British as a League of Nations.

In 1967, following independence, the government invited Canadian firm Project Planning Associates Ltd to draw up a master plan to help control and organise the then capital of the country, Dar es Salaam, which.
The plan was cancelled in 1972, in part due to its failure to adequately address the historical and social problems associated with the city.

In 1974, after a nationwide party referendum, the Tanzanian government announced that the capital would be moved from Dar es Salaam to a more central location to create significant social and economic improvements for.

The official capital since 1996, Dodoma was envisaged as the first non-monumental capital city as opposed to the monumentality and hierarchy of other planned capital cities such as Abuja, Yamoussoukro, Brasília and Washington, D.C.
